title: Hacking Web Servers

objectives.text: Describe how Apache, nginx and IIS handle requests (document root, virtual hosts, worker processes, application pools, reverse proxies)
Spot the common web server misconfigurations: verbose banners, directory listing, status pages, sample content, risky HTTP methods
Recognize web server attack classes from a log line or scenario (traversal, response splitting, cache poisoning, smuggling, DoS, DNS hijacking, defacement, web shells)
Map web server attacks to MITRE ATT&CK (T1190, T1505.003, T1498, T1499.002, T1491.002, T1110) and name the matching detection
Put EC-Council's web server attack methodology in order and name the tool used at each step
Harden a web server using NIST SP 800-44, CIS Benchmarks and the Apache, nginx and IIS directives that matter
Explain patch management with NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4 (risk responses, maintenance plans, verify and monitor) and CISA KEV prioritization
Choose detection controls for web server compromise: file integrity monitoring, log review, process lineage, WAF

readingMap.why: Know the three servers' moving parts and the default settings that leak information; skip the long architecture diagrams.
Most questions describe an attack and ask for its name: learn the one clue that identifies each class.
Step order and tool-to-step matching (banner grabbing, mirroring, directory brute forcing, Nikto) are frequent tool questions.
Hardening directives, patch management terms and detection controls come up in scenario questions; skim long tool lists.

labs.name: Fingerprint and audit your own local web server
labs.skill: Banner grabbing with curl and Nmap, running Nikto and http-methods against a server you own, then fixing what they report

labs.name: Harden Apache or nginx and re-test
labs.skill: ServerTokens/server_tokens, TraceEnable, directory listing, status pages, request timeouts; compare scan results before and after

labs.name: Check a TLS configuration against the Mozilla guideline
labs.skill: Generating a modern TLS config and verifying protocols, ciphers and HSTS with testssl.sh on your own server

labs.name: Practice path traversal and information disclosure labs
labs.skill: Recognizing traversal and information-leak responses in a legal training environment

feynmanPrompts: Explain to a new sysadmin why a web server that answers with its exact version, lists folders and keeps sample files is easier to attack, and what three settings you would change first.
Tell the difference between DNS server hijacking, website defacement and web cache poisoning using one short story for each, and say where a defender would notice each one.
A critical web server flaw is announced and exploited, but the patch needs a week of testing. Walk through what you would do that week using NIST SP 800-40 terms.
